label: The Planar Shape Space
notes: Across printed pages 87 to 109 the planar case stands apart because two dimensions identify with the complex line. We preview the whole arc: complex preshape, the quotient by rotation giving complex projective space, the Fubini-Study metric, the Veronese-Whitney embedding, and the resulting extrinsic mean.

label: Landmarks as a Complex Vector
notes: A planar configuration of k labelled landmarks becomes one complex vector once each point is read as a complex number. Centering removes translation, so the configuration lives in a complex hyperplane of dimension k minus one, the natural arena before scale and rotation are quotiented away.

label: Complex Preshape Sphere
notes: Dividing the centered complex vector by its Hermitian norm removes scale and lands us on the unit sphere inside complex Euclidean space of dimension k minus one. This complex preshape sphere is the stage on which the rotation group will act by unit-modulus scalar multiplication.

label: Rotation as Complex Phase
notes: In the plane a rotation by an angle multiplies every landmark by a single unit complex number. So the whole rotation orbit of a preshape is the circle of unit scalars times that vector. Quotienting by this circle is precisely the Hopf-style construction behind projective space.

label: Shape Space is CP^{k-2}
notes: Collapsing each phase circle on the complex preshape sphere identifies the planar shape space with complex projective space of complex dimension k minus two. Every shape is a complex line through the origin, a clean and beautiful manifold with no singular strata in the planar case.

label: Fubini-Study Geometry
notes: Complex projective space carries the canonical Fubini-Study Riemannian metric descended from the round sphere. It makes the planar shape space a homogeneous, constant holomorphic sectional curvature manifold, the geometric backbone for measuring how far apart two planar shapes truly are.

label: Procrustes Distance
notes: The Fubini-Study geodesic distance between two shapes is the Procrustes distance: the arccosine of the modulus of the Hermitian inner product of unit representatives. It optimally aligns one configuration onto the other over all rotations and reports the residual angular separation between the complex lines.

label: Geodesics on CP^{k-2}
notes: Geodesics of the Fubini-Study metric are images of great circles on the preshape sphere that stay orthogonal to the phase fibers. Walking a horizontal great circle and projecting down traces the shortest shape path, the curve realizing the Procrustes distance between two planar configurations.

label: Veronese-Whitney Embedding
notes: For extrinsic analysis we embed each shape into Hermitian matrices by sending a unit representative z to the rank-one projection z times z conjugate transpose. This map is well defined on lines, equivariant under rotation and relabelling, and isometric enough to carry the Fubini-Study structure faithfully.

label: The Mean Hermitian Matrix
notes: Averaging the embedded projection matrices over a sample gives a single mean Hermitian matrix in linear space. This Euclidean average generally leaves the embedded image, so it must be projected back to the nearest rank-one projection to return a legitimate planar shape.

label: Extrinsic Mean is Top Eigenvector
notes: The closest rank-one projection to the mean Hermitian matrix is the projection onto its leading eigenvector. Hence the extrinsic, or Veronese-Whitney, mean shape is exactly the top eigenvector of the average of z times z conjugate transpose, a fast and unique estimator under a simple eigengap.

label: Intrinsic vs Extrinsic Means
notes: The intrinsic mean minimizes squared Fubini-Study distance and needs iteration, while the extrinsic mean solves a one-shot eigenproblem. Both admit central limit theorems in tangent coordinates, but the extrinsic version yields cleaner asymptotic covariances and the bootstrap confidence regions used in practice.

label: Application and Recap
notes: On real landmark data the eigen-mean and its bootstrap pivot give two-sample tests for shape difference. We recap the route: complex preshape, quotient to CP^{k-2}, Fubini-Study and Procrustes geometry, Veronese-Whitney embedding, and the eigenvector extrinsic mean with its central limit theorem.
